problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)={x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}-25x+125$ have multiplicity $2?$
worked_solution:
First, we need to factor the polynomial. For this polynomial, we can factor by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & ={x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}-25x+125 \\  & ={x}^{2}(x-5)-25(x-5) \\  & =({x}^{2}-25)(x-5) \\  & =(x+5)(x-5)(x-5) \\  & =(x-5{)}^{2}(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

To find the roots and their multiplicities, we look at the factors:

- The factor $(x-5)$ has an exponent of $2$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=5$ has multiplicity $2.$

- The factor $(x+5)$ has an exponent of $1$ in the factored form of $p(x).$ So the root $x=-5$ has multiplicity $1.$

In conclusion, only the root $x=5$ has multiplicity $2.$
